MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  April 26, 2022
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library
Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Bucknum
at 5:00 p.m., on April 26, 2022, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by
5:00 p.m. on April 21, 2022, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted at
the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Raths
  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs
  Mayor Bucknum

Absent:  Council Member Goodell

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk
  Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

Conference with Legal Counsel—Existing Litigation (Paragraph (1) of Subdivision (d) Of
Section 54956.9) Name of Case: (Michael Schlesinger v. City of Mission Viejo)

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:02 p.m., Mayor Bucknum recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:01 p.m. with four City Council Members present and Council Member
Goodell absent.

City Council Minutes  1  April 26, 2022
 REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Curley announced there was one item in closed session. An update was given to
Council, and Council gave staff further direction.

INVOCATION: Council Member Kelley

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Pro Tem Sachs

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Proclaim May 2022 To Be Mental Health Awareness Month

  Mayor Bucknum presented Proclamation to Amy Betonte with Extraordinary Lives
  Foundation.

P2. Orange County Finance Housing Trust Update

  Received presentation from Adam Eliason.

P3. Presentation by True North Research on the Results from the Community Survey

  Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Addressed the survey and stated, that in this case, the hidden agenda is
  for increased taxes. She mentioned that the results are used to manipulate the public, and gave
  an example of the opposition of California Voting Rights Act for the Councils gain. She
  referenced numerous statistics and misleading data, in her opinion, such as the satisfaction of
  City services, and the Garden Plaza. She concluded by stating she will continue with her
  remarks under Public Comments.

  Received presentation from Timothy McLarney.

CITY MANAGER REPORT (taken out of order)

12. Police Chief Update

  City Manager Wilberg informed everyone that Police Chief, Captain Quyen Vuong has been
  transferred to Headquarters to head up a special unit, and a new Police Chief shall be appointed
  next week. Mayor Bucknum recognized outgoing Captain Vuong by presenting him with a
  Proclamation. Mayor Pro Tem Sachs and Fire Chief Capobianco also shared their appreciation
  of Captain Vuong, and presented him with a few parting gifts. Captain Vuong thanked the
  City Council and Staff for the opportunity of serving this wonderful City.

At 7:18 pm Mayor Bucknum took a 12-minute recess.

City Council Minutes  2  April 26, 2022
 At 7:30 pm Mayor Bucknum reconvened the meeting.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Nancy Van Deusen, M.V.: Referenced the April 11, 2022 Planning and Transportation Commission
Meeting addressing the issue of affordable housing. She raised a number of points including;
Mission Viejo being the most affordable City in Orange County, and concluded by requesting the
Council keep the current zoning as office professional.

Tom Moore, M.V.: Spoke on Council Policy #0600-06 and the unsightly Campaign signs seen on
the streets of Mission Viejo when approaching an election, and suggested a staff member monitor
the compliance of this policy. He also referenced Senate Bill 946 and the need to place limitations
and restrictions on street vendors.

Cathy Palmer, M.V.: Asked Trish Kelley, as Brian Goodell was not present, to run for reelection in
2022, and referenced the two-year period on the candidate statements. She also mentioned that she
still has an unanswered questioned with regards to the terms. Lastly, her advice to Council Member
Goodell and Kelley in Districts 2 & 4, was to take advantage of good impression made on residents
in opposition to Value Rock and appear on ballot in 2022.

Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Continued with her comments on the Community Survey results, including
increase in taxes, and bringing cannabis businesses in Mission Viejo. She mentioned the pending
lawsuit to remove Council from office, and referred to the City Council’s manipulation of the
Garden Plaza Project.

Mary Wathen, M.V.: Shared her concern and safety associated with ebikes. Asked if there are any
guidelines, or if there is an ordinance set in place with regards to where they can be ridden, how
fast they can go, and if basic bike safety rules apply. She concluded by asking if there is any
consideration of a bike trail along Oso Creek Trail and by the future Paseo.

Rebekah Earnest, M.V.: Thanked the Council for moving the Garden Plaza project along, and stated
that an incident at the plaza prompted her to bring the deterioration and various code violations to
the Council’s attention. She asked that the City Council follow the Planning and Transportation
Commission and reject Value Rocks request for mixed use zoning.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  Goodell

City Council Minutes  3  April 26, 2022
 1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes from the regular City Council Meeting of April 12, 2022, as presented.

2.  Check Register Dated April 1, 2022 in the Amount of $488,716.40

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  Check Register Dated April 8, 2022 in the Amount of $2,574,384.18

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Renewal of Managed Detection and Response Security Services

  Approved purchase order to Nth Generation in amount not to exceed $69,842.69 for annual
  renewal of Arctic Wolf Managed Detection and Response security services.

5.  Renewal of Firewall Security Subscription

  Approved purchase order for Cisco Firewall security subscription annual renewal to Resilient
  Communications Inc. in the amount of $36,799.50.

6.  Renewal of Email Security Solution

  Approved purchase order to Optiv Security Inc. in amount not to exceed $31,102.36 for
  ProofPoint Email Security Solution and Support.

7.  2022 Orange County International Triathlon in Mission Viejo

  Approved the request submitted by Gemini Timing to hold the 2022 Orange County
  International Triathlon in Mission Viejo on Sunday, May 22, 2022.

8.  Draft 2022-2023 Annual Action Plan Detailing the Proposed Use of Community
  Development Block Grant Funds

  Adopted Resolution 22-08 approving the City's 2022-2023 Annual Action Plan detailing the
  proposed use of Community Development Block Grant Funds, and authorizing submission of
  the plan to the United States Department of Housing and Urban Development.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

City Council Minutes  4  April 26, 2022
 OLD BUSINESS

9.  Community Choice Energy Update

  Receive update from Assistant City Manager Keith Rattay.

  Mayor Bucknum asked staff for a presentation from Mr. Brian Probolsky of Moulton Niguel
  Water District (MNWD) at a future Council meeting.

Ed Maurer, M.V.: Spoke on Community Choice Energy and referred to other Cities in Orange
County that are participating in these programs. He encouraged staff and Council to inform
residents on Orange County Power Authority (OCPA). He concluded by stating he was surprised
the City survey did not ask any questions pertaining to climate change.

Helen Maurer, M.V.: Was pleased to hear the Community Choice Energy update and asked staff
and Council to not let this project and investigation languish. She added that this is an important
issue, and the City needs to be proactive.

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

10. Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) Report

  Receive report from Council Member Raths.

11. Local Agency Formation Commission Orange County (LAFCO) Report

  Receive report from Mayor Bucknum.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

13. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley stated it has been a busy week. She attended the OCSD Medal of Valor
luncheon ceremony, and added what an amazing leader Captain Quyen Vuong is and how much he
is appreciated in Mission Viejo. That she attended Marine Lake Day for the City’s Adopted Marine
Battalion, the Grand opening of Amazon Fresh, a bench dedication for Mr. Paul at Riley Elementary
School, and Earth and Arbor Day. She commended staff and Director of Public Services Jerry Hill
on a great job. She also read a portion of a letter received from Providence Mission Hospital, stating
that Newsweek had recognized them as the number one Hospital in Orange County for the second

City Council Minutes  5  April 26, 2022
 year in a row. To conclude, Council Member Kelley announced that on Sunday, May 1, from 1 -
4pm will be Water Safety Day at Marguerite Aquatics Center.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths congratulated Chief of Police Quyen Vuong for all he has done for the City
of Mission Viejo in keeping the residents safe, and added that he is one of the finest Captains that
he has had the pleasure to work with. He gave an update on the Post Office, which is a working
progress. And lastly, he also attended Marine Lake Day and thanked the Marines and Sailors
Adoption Committee for all their hard work.

Mayor Pro Tem Sachs

Mayor Pro Tem Sachs asked staff to invite parents as well as children to the ebike training, when it
takes place.

Mayor Bucknum

Mayor Bucknum reminded everyone that on Thursday, May 12, the Community Townhall on Sober
Living Homes is taking place at 6pm in the Council Chamber. She announced that she shall be
conducting some coffee/outreach events in conjunction with local businesses throughout the year.
Mayor Bucknum stated she is pleased with the Community Survey, how it is a good form of hearing
from residents and how it helps guide the Council in their decision making. She shared the
following upcoming events; Sunday, May 22, Triathlon at the Lake from 7-10am, and on Saturday,
May 14, E‐Waste & Household Hazardous Waste Collection Event at the City Hall Parking Lot
from 9-110am. Tomorrow is a huge day for the homeless, and Mayor Bucknum encouraged
residents to visit Homemade OC, a large entity that partners with Families Forward and Mercy
House who are holding a one-day fundraiser. She mentioned Assembly Bill ~ AB2011 Buffy Wicks
~ Affordable Housing and High Roads Jobs Act of 2022; and that the City sent a letter of opposition
and asked resident to make a comment against this Bill as it will take away their rights to speak and
have a say as to what happens in our City. She concluded by wishing everyone a Happy Mother’s
Day for Sunday, May 8.

ADJOURNMENT AT 8:42 P.M. TO TUESDAY, MAY 10, 2022, AT 5:00 P.M.

______________________________________________
Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of May 10, 2022

City Council Minutes  6  April 26, 2022
